title: Elastic pocket scaling and tenant fairness PRD (wip)
body:
Summary:

This doc sketches a complementary autoscaling and burst model for Redwood Dedicated called 'Elastic Pockets' aimed at improving tenant throughput predictability while enabling controlled bursts and stronger tenant fairness during demand surges. The idea: each tenant has a baseline reserved pocket (steady-state capacity) and an elastic pool of short-lived micro-pockets that can be allocated on demand with policy-driven priority, cost signals, and isolation guardrails.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce 99th-percentile latency violations for Dedicated customers under moderate-to-high contention by 30% vs current baseline.
- Provide transparent, auditable burst events with tenant-level billing/credits and observable fallbacks.
- Ensure noisy neighbor events do not cause cascading evictions of stable tenants; target <5% incident rate where eviction required for stable tenants during major surges.
- Give operators simple controls to tune aggressiveness (concurrency, burst window, credit reuse) and an ops playbook for incident triage.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not propose new hardware or a fleet re-architecture. It focuses on control-plane policies, admission/enforcement logic, and observable signals.

User stories / personas:
- Platform SRE: needs clear metrics and runbooks to detect and mitigate unfair burst consumption.
- Tenant (product engineering): wants predictable baseline throughput but occasional ability to burst for spikes without manual capacity purchases.
- Sales/Account Exec: wants to offer a burst add-on (pay-as-you-go credits) with SLAs for baseline and non-SLA best-effort bursts.
- Solutions Eng: needs feature flags and config knobs to demo tenancy isolation and credit behavior.

Key concepts and terminology:
- Pocket: a unit of reserved capacity (e.g., N concurrent inference pipelines or X tokens/sec equivalence) owned by a tenant as steady-state.
- Elastic micro-pocket: a transient allocation from a shared elastic pool, short TTL (default 60s) intended for absorbing spikes.
- Burst credits: per-tenant accounting units consumed when using elastic micro-pockets; can be prepaid or billed post-pay.
- Admission controller: probabilistic controller that admits/rejects requests into elastic micro-pockets based on policy, tenant credits, and global load.
- Fairness ledger: a time-series that tracks recent pocket usage per tenant and feeds admission decisions to avoid long-term unfairness.

Design overview (high level):
1) Baseline assignment: tenants continue to have reserved pockets (unchanged). Baseline SLOs apply to pocket capacity.
2) Elastic pool: a cluster-level shared capacity that operators size (configurable by region/cluster). This pool serves micro-pockets on demand.
3) Admission & scoring: each burst request is assigned a score computed from: tenant priority tier, remaining burst credits, recent usage (ledger), and global load factor. A threshold-based probabilistic admission decides whether to grant a micro-pocket. Thresholds are soft and can vary by cluster SLO.
4) Isolation controls: when cluster load crosses thresholds, we stop admitting low-priority tenants first (graceful knob). In addition, auto-quarantine isolates tenants who repeatedly exceed ephemeral throttles.
5) Credit model: three options supported: pay-as-you-go billing, prepaid burst credits (discounted), and a limited free buffer included with reserved pockets.
6) Fallbacks: if admission denied or micro-pocket evicted mid-flight, requests are routed to: a) baseline pocket if available, b) a cheaper/quantized model variant, or c) a best-effort queue with retry/backoff.

Policy primitives (operators & product knobs):
- pocket-size (per-tenant baseline)
- micro-pocket-ttl (default 30–120s)
- admission-sensitivity (aggressive | balanced | conservative)
- fairness-window (sliding window for ledger, default 15m)
- quarantine-threshold (events per window)
- credit-replenish-rate (for prepaid buckets)

Metrics and observability (required):
- pocket-utilization per tenant (p50/p95/p99)
- micro-pocket-grants / denials per tenant and per cluster
- burst-credit-burn rate and balance per tenant
- fallbacks invoked (counts, latencies, routes chosen)
- fairness-imbalance score (0..1) showing disparity across tenants
- incidents where baseline tenants were evicted due to bursts
- dashboard: per-tenant timeline with grants, denials, evictions, and credits

Operational playbook (concise):
- Detection: alert when cluster micro-pocket-denial-rate > 5% for 5m or fairness-imbalance > 0.3
- Triage: query fairness ledger for top consumers, correlate with request traces and model mix; identify if single tenant or many tenants.
- Mitigation: temporarily tighten admission-sensitivity to conservative; evict long-running micro-pockets from offenders; open a prioritized throttling ticket for anomalous tenant.
- Recovery: re-enable normal sensitivity after 15m and reconcile credits/billing adjustments for impacted customers if needed.

Implementation notes and constraints:
- Admission controller needs to be placed at the per-request front door (gateway) for low-latency decisions; prefer an in-memory sliding ledger with consistent hashing to approximate global view.
- Avoid synchronous global consensus on each grant (stale local view acceptable if correctness is probabilistic).
- Must integrate with existing model fallback routing (console + runtime) and with billing/usage pipelines for credit accounting.
- Backwards compatible: tenants without burst credits should still be allowed the small free buffer and then denied to baseline fallbacks.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: fairness algorithm could starve newly onboarded tenants. Mitigation: add bootstrapping credits and a soft ramp.
- Risk: micro-pocket churn increases scheduling overhead. Mitigation: default TTL and reuse heuristics (co-locate micro-pockets for same tenant if successive grants).
- Risk: billing disputes from transient evictions. Mitigation: keep an audit log of grant/eviction events and build an automated bill-adjust flow for clearly failed bursts.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is the canonical size of a pocket? tokens/sec, concurrency, GPU-share? (engineering to propose measurable unit)
- Should fairness-imbalance be exposed to tenants via console? (privacy vs transparency tradeoff)
- Fine-grained pricing: how to price micro-pockets that execute on cheaper quantized models vs full-precision runs?
- Need a prototype of admission scoring (simulator using summer 2025 production traces).

Migration and rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (experiment): simulator + offline scoring on a 2-week historical window; measure fairness and denial rates.
- Phase 1 (canary): enable elastic pool in one cluster with internal tenants only; conservative admission-sensitivity; collect metrics for 2 weeks.
- Phase 2 (beta): customer opt-in with small prepaid credits; add console toggles and billing hooks.
- Phase 3 (general): default on for new tenants; migration tooling for converting legacy reservations into pockets with a recommended mapping.

Appendix (notes & references):
- Related tickets: JIRA-DEDI-421 (admission controller), JIRA-DEDI-480 (billing credits schema).
- Reference implementations: prototype in runtime repo: PR 834 (link above).
- Sample operator CLI: rdedicated pocket list | grant-credit | set-admission-sensitivity

Draft notes / author thoughts: 
- I want to keep the initial admission simple (score -> threshold) and iterate to a bandit-style controller later.
- We should try a TTL of 60s initially and capture churn metrics before reducing TTL.
- Consider a tiny per-tenant probation window after a quarantine period to avoid oscillation.

Action items (owners):
- Marcus: build simulator and run against Oct–Nov traces (ETA 2025-11-20)
- Ben: mock billing schema and add credit usage events to usage-pipeline (ETA 2025-11-30)
- Sofia: draft console UX for credits and per-tenant timeline (ETA 2025-12-05)
- Asha: finalize operator controls and draft SRE runbook (ETA 2025-12-10)

Status: WIP — want feedback on admission scoring formula and whether to include a temporary free buffer per tenant.
